title: When the Confession Wakes
premise: Quentin Eastwick, the coroner of the river town of Marrow's Bend, recognizes the dead man's clothes as his own — stolen from his closet while he slept. The victim, a retired judge, clutched a page of a family ledger that Quentin slowly realizes maps every bribe and buried crime committed by the town's founding families, including his own late father. As more bodies surface dressed in Quentin's belongings — a killer staging him for a fall — he must decode the ledger before the true heir to its secrets silences him too. In the end, Quentin chooses justice outside the law: he publishes the ledger at the judge's funeral rather than hand it to the compromised sheriff, exposing the conspiracy and clearing his name, though it costs him his badge and wins him an unexpected ally in the witness who first found the body.
about_author: Tamsin Galloway is the pen name of a former rural court reporter who spent a decade transcribing small-town inquests before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries steeped in the quiet rot of close-knit communities, where everyone knows everyone's grave but no one knows their sins.

chapters.title: The Suit He Buried His Father In
chapters.summary: Quentin Eastwick examines the body of retired Judge Ambrose Pell, found by schoolteacher Nora Vane on the riverbank — and freezes: the man wears Quentin's own charcoal suit, missing from his closet that morning. POV: Quentin. The emotional beat is cold dread; the personal violation transforms routine duty into a hunt, and Sheriff Dawes's too-quick ruling of accidental drowning smells like cover-up.

chapters.title: A Ledger Written in Family Ink
chapters.summary: Searching the judge's chambers, Quentin finds a torn ledger page listing dates, sums, and initials — including 'Q.E.' entries predating his birth, implicating his father. POV alternates between Quentin and Nora, who admits she saw someone fleeing in clothes identical to Quentin's. The beat is mounting paranoia: someone is dressing the dead in Quentin's life, stitching him into a pattern he can't yet read.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: A second body — the town clerk — again in Quentin's clothing, forces Dawes to name Quentin a suspect. Decoding the ledger with Nora, Quentin traces it to the Eastwick estate's foundation: his father laundered bribes for the founding families, and Judge Pell was the last living co-signer. POV: Nora, watching Quentin choose truth over blood. The climax ignites when the killer — the judge's own nephew, heir to the secrets — corners them at the records vault.

chapters.title: Read Aloud at the Graveside
chapters.summary: Quenton survives the vault confrontation, subduing the nephew with Nora's help, but realizes the sheriff is implicated too. Rather than surrender the ledger to law that will bury it, he reads it aloud at Judge Pell's funeral before the whole town. POV: Quentin. The resolution balances cost and grace — his badge gone, his father's name ruined, but his own cleared, and Nora beside him as the town begins, at last, to dig up its truths.
